title: The Sleep Lab
hook: I watch strangers sleep for a living. One rule: if a patient sits up and stares into the camera... don't go in.
lines: I work nights at a sleep clinic, watching strangers sleep on six small screens.
The tech who trained me left one rule.
If a patient ever sits up and stares into the camera... don't go in. Don't use the intercom. Just wait.
For two months, all I saw was snoring.
Then, at three a.m., the man in room six sat up.
Slowly. Like something was lifting him by the collar.
He turned to the camera, and he didn't blink. His lips were moving.
I turned up the room audio.
He was counting down. Five... four...
Room five sat up. Then room four. Then three. Then two.
All of them, staring at me. All of them counting.
I kept my hands flat on the desk, and I didn't breathe.
That's when I remembered. There are only five patient rooms.
Screen one is the camera above my desk... and on it, I wasn't sitting alone.
